records.subject: User-approved Ambrosius Benson Salvator Mundi; preserve selection
records.title: Salvator Mundi

physicalObject.source: Christie's London Old Masters Evening Sale, 3 December 2019, lot 4
physicalObject.custody: Fundación Cultural Formación y Humanismo listed as vendor; current physical location not independently established

imageRoute.frameStatus: Auction catalogue reports inventory no. 9 on frame; actual source-file frame inclusion requires native inspection

records.identityCaution: Christie's catalogue distinguishes Savior iconography from papal-tiara attributes of God the Father, suggesting deliberately ambiguous identification; preserve approved editorial choice without asserting theological exclusivity. Do not confuse with KMSKA collection 241 or Rubens collection 302, both separate artworks.
records.summaryEn: The approved Benson Salvator Mundi can be linked to the exact 91.4 × 86.1 cm panel catalogued by Christie's in December 2019. A 2,987 × 3,200 Commons image exists, but its auction-photograph rights, frame-free presentation and native quality remain uncertified.
records.summaryFr: Le Salvator Mundi de Benson déjà approuvé correspond au panneau de 91,4 × 86,1 cm catalogué par Christie's en décembre 2019. Une image Commons de 2 987 × 3 200 pixels existe, mais les droits de la photographie de vente, l'absence de cadre et la qualité native restent à vérifier.

records.subject: User-approved Ludovico Carracci An Angel Frees the Souls of Purgatory
records.title: An Angel Frees the Souls of Purgatory

physicalObject.accession: Not independently obtained from Vatican custodian

records.identityCaution: Published object dimensions 44 high × 51 wide imply landscape while Commons JPEG 866 wide × 1200 high is portrait. Do not resolve by rotating/cropping/upscaling or certifying. Obtain custodial catalogue/inventory and compare approved preview to original.
records.summaryEn: The existing All Souls selection remains held: the commonly circulated 866 × 1,200 reproduction is portrait-oriented, while independent catalogues report a 44 × 51 cm canvas. The discrepancy requires physical-object and image-orientation reconciliation before any master is certified.
records.summaryFr: L'œuvre déjà retenue pour les fidèles défunts reste en attente : la reproduction courante de 866 × 1 200 pixels est verticale, alors que les catalogues indiquent une toile de 44 × 51 cm. Cette divergence doit être résolue avant toute validation du visuel principal.

records.subject: Jean Baptiste de Champaigne Martyrdom of Saint Lawrence; already in 281-candidate and 451-work sources
records.title: The Martyrdom of Saint Lawrence
records.identityCaution: The bulk intake also has an ART- alias with old 103596 URL and matching artist/title, but this URL was not independently resolved. Treat as probable same-object alias pending accession crosswalk, not a second artwork. Museum's current attribution is Jean Baptiste de Champaigne, despite historical inscription P DE CHAMPAIGNE and older Philippe attribution.
records.summaryEn: The existing Saint Lawrence candidate is now tied to NGA accession 1998.68.1 and a directly linked public-domain IIIF download. An older catalogue URL and Philippe de Champaigne attribution must be reconciled as possible aliases, not counted as a new painting.
records.summaryFr: Le candidat existant pour saint Laurent est désormais rattaché à l'inventaire NGA 1998.68.1 et à une image IIIF libre de droits. Une ancienne URL et l'attribution historique à Philippe de Champaigne restent à rapprocher sans créer une nouvelle œuvre.

records.subject: Saint Sebastian succored by angel and possible Saint Irene
records.title: Saint Sebastian
records.identityCaution: NGA records an earlier Rubens attribution changed to Tanzio; woman may be Saint Irene, not definitively. Distinct from existing Rubens and Marco d'Oggiono Sebastian candidates.
records.summaryEn: Tanzio's 1620s Saint Sebastian is a dark Caravaggesque oil painting showing an angel removing an arrow while a woman, possibly Saint Irene, supports the martyr. The NGA identifies the exact original and offers a public-domain image.
records.summaryFr: Le Saint Sébastien de Tanzio, peint vers 1620–1630 dans un clair-obscur caravagesque, montre un ange retirant une flèche tandis qu'une femme, peut-être sainte Irène, soutient le martyr. La NGA identifie l'original et propose une image libre.

records.subject: Conversion of Saint Paul, Acts 9
records.title: The Conversion of Saint Paul
records.identityCaution: Distinct from previously researched Murillo and Rubens/Diepenbeeck Conversion of Paul. Landscape 152.7 × 236.3 cm, dense horses and figures; portrait phone crop would remove essential narrative. No automatic hero recommendation.
records.summaryEn: Tintoretto's Conversion of Saint Paul, circa 1544, illustrates Acts 9 with a crowded landscape of frightened horses and soldiers. Its NGA original has an open image route, but the horizontal narrative is a serious mobile-crop constraint.
records.summaryFr: La Conversion de saint Paul du Tintoret, vers 1544, illustre les Actes 9 par une scène horizontale peuplée de chevaux et de soldats effrayés. L'image NGA est libre, mais la composition très large pose un problème de cadrage mobile.

records.subject: Saint Jerome and angel with trumpet
records.title: Saint Jerome and the Angel

imageRoute.previewNote: Web-rendered image appears frame-free with dark background; not native image QA

records.identityCaution: NGA Barberini inventory analysis explicitly separates a vertical unidentified saint, a square Saint Jerome, and the horizontal Vouet Saint Jerome in its collection. Never merge these three physical works.
records.summaryEn: Vouet's shadowed Saint Jerome and the Angel depicts the Doctor writing as an angel raises a trumpet. NGA accession 1961.9.52 is distinguishable from two similarly described Barberini pictures; its horizontal layout requires mobile review.
records.summaryFr: Le Saint Jérôme et l'ange de Vouet représente le Docteur écrivant dans l'ombre, tandis qu'un ange tient une trompette. L'inventaire NGA 1961.9.52 se distingue de deux autres tableaux Barberini similaires ; son format horizontal demande un contrôle mobile.

records.subject: Saint Stephen martyrdom in a historical Roman Missal initial
records.title: Historiated Initial (E) Excised from the Colonna Missal: The Martyrdom of Saint Stephen

physicalObject.medium: ink, tempera and liquid gold on vellum

records.identityCaution: The miniature is within the ornamental letter E, not a full-size oil painting. CMA links it directly to the Offertory Elegerunt Apostoli Stephanum for the December 26 Mass. Strong liturgical documentary image; not a substitute for a dark-Baroque hero.
records.summaryEn: A circa-1532 Roman missal initial depicts Saint Stephen's stoning within the letter E that introduces the Offertory of his December 26 Mass. This exact liturgical connection makes it valuable for a historical missal illustration, not necessarily a hero image.
records.summaryFr: Une initiale enluminée d'un missel romain, vers 1532, représente la lapidation de saint Étienne dans la lettre E ouvrant l'offertoire de sa messe du 26 décembre. Le lien liturgique est exact, mais l'image relève plutôt de l'illustration historique que d'un visuel principal.

records.subject: Saint Anne with Holy Family; related subject not single-saint portrait
records.title: Holy Family with Saint Anne

physicalObject.institution: Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York

imageRoute.rights: Met object marked Public Domain; institution CC0 open access

records.identityCaution: Distinct from B19 Trevisani sketch and other Rubens Anne works; French painter remains unidentified. Exact Saint Anne appears but multi-person Holy Family composition does not constitute exclusive Anne portrait.
records.summaryEn: This early-seventeenth-century French Holy Family with Saint Anne, Met accession 1976.100.12, is a compact portrait-oriented Caravaggesque composition. It is an open-access related-subject alternative for Saint Anne, not a newly approved feast master.
records.summaryFr: Cette Sainte Famille avec sainte Anne, œuvre française du début du XVIIe siècle conservée au Met sous le numéro 1976.100.12, présente un clair-obscur sur un format vertical. C'est une alternative iconographique liée à sainte Anne, non un visuel de fête approuvé.
